text:
maria (sales): Quick thread — Mediflow execs asked for a clear capacity plan we can paste into their security questionnaire and procurement. They gave a traffic profile and SLOs: steady 120 qps, peak 420 qps for short bursts (3–5m), gen size ~140 tokens/request, p99 latency target <= 250ms for user-facing LLM completions. They want recommended reserved GPU counts, autoscale policy (how we handle bursts), and a fallback model that keeps UX acceptable if capacity is constrained. Can we get numbers + a short snippet to drop into their questionnaire?

aj (solutions): Are those qps numbers end-to-end requests/sec or individual model calls? Also which model family are they planning to use? (customer mentioned "open-70b-ish" but not locked).

maria (sales): Good point — customer said they'd prefer a 70B-class foundation for quality, but is open to 13B for bursts. The qps above is end-to-end requests/sec from the app (one model call per request).

devon (eng): Back-of-envelope: for a 70B quantized model (8-bit, KV cache): one high-end A100-class GPU (our medium perf profile) can sustain ~35–60 concurrent requests depending on seq len and batching; realistic steady-state RPS for 140 tokens @ 1s-ish per request = ~1 rps per GPU without batching. With batching and continuous batching we can push to ~12–18 rps per GPU at 140 tokens while keeping p99 under 250ms if latency SLO is soft. For production SLA with p99<=250ms and predictable tail, we should size conservatively. Recommendation:
- Reserved baseline: 24 x GPU for steady + headroom. (This assumes autoscale can add burst GPUs).
- Autoscale policy: keep target utilization ~55–65%; scale up when average queue latency > 50ms for 30s or when CPU/gpu util breaches 70%. Scale step: add GPUs in increments of 4; cool down 2m.
- Burst buffer: prewarm 8 GPUs (burst credit) to handle 3–5m 420 qps spikes. The prewarm should be in the same AZs as traffic.
- Fallback model: route ~50% of traffic to a 13B-quantized variant (2–3x cheaper per token) under sustained >3m over-provision conditions. Use sampling to route 10% initially to verify quality.
Estimated steady math (very rough): assume 15 rps/GPU => steady 120 qps -> 8 GPUs; but for p99 tail safety and customer enterprise needs we recommend 24 reserved, which buys runway, and lets autoscale reduce infra noise while meeting SLO.

katie (sre): Couple practical notes:
- Distribute reserved GPUs across 3 AZs (8/8/8) to tolerate AZ failure and satisfy their audit requirement.
- Add a canary route for new model variants and quantized weights; don't flip on fallback globally without 1-hour canary.
- For the security questionnaire they specifically ask "max sustained requests/minute, max observed burst, expected p95/p99 and retention window" — give them a short block they can paste.
- Also note: if they require FedRAMP-like logging/retention we need to list prewarming and retention impacts (billing and audit).

maria (sales): Perfect. Can someone give the concise snippet (one-paragraph + 4-line bullets) I can paste into the questionnaire? Make it copy-paste friendly.

devon (eng): Snippet for questionnaire: "Redwood will provision a production footprint sized for Mediflow's profile: steady-state 120 requests/sec, peak instantaneous bursts up to 420 requests/sec (3–5 minute windows). Expected generation size ~140 tokens/request. Baseline reserved capacity: 24 GPUs (distributed across 3 AZs) with autoscaling enabled to add GPUs in +4 increments when queue latency or GPU utilization exceed thresholds. Prewarmed burst pool: 8 GPUs for short spikes. Fallback policy: traffic can be routed to a quantized 13B model when sustained overload is detected; canary testing and gradual rollout used before fallbacks. Expected latency: median ~50–120ms, p95 ~150–200ms, p99 <= 250ms for sized configuration. Data retention and logging will follow our standard enterprise package (retention window and audit logs configurable per contract)."

aj (solutions): Nice. For pricing arm, finance wants an approximate monthly cost delta for 24 reserved GPUs vs 8 baseline plus autoscale. Can you give a quick monthly ballpark? We don't need exact invoice-ready numbers, just a range to flag in procurement.

devon (eng): Ballpark: assuming a reserved GPU unit rate (example) of $6k/GPU/month for the reserved tier -> 24 GPUs ~= $144k/mo. If we instead keep 8 reserved GPUs ($48k/mo) + autoscale to peak using on-demand @ ~1.6x cost, monthly could be ~48k + variable burst spend (30–80k) depending on spike frequency -> say $80–130k/mo. Note: quantized 13B fallback lowers token-cost and can materially reduce burst charges by ~35–50% depending on mix.

ops-bot (bot): Created ticket INF-4321: mediflow-capacity-prewarm (owner: devon). Linked to sales-op:MEDIFLOW-2023.

maria (sales): Thanks — last asks: 1) Can we get a short load test command to share with Mediflow for their POC so they can run a synthetic and show us realistic spikes? 2) Who owns the questionnaire section (I will paste it but need an engineering signature).

aj (solutions): Use a vegeta quick command or our internal runner. Example (vegeta):
```
echo 'GET http://redwood-poc-endpoint/v1/generate' | vegeta attack -duration=5m -rate=450 | vegeta report
```
Recommend they ramp 50 -> 200 -> 420 over 3 phases and run at each for 3 minutes to validate autoscale.

devon (eng): I'll own the questionnaire section and will sign off once the canary numbers are in. I'll also add a small harness snippet for their infra team to run against our staging endpoints (will paste into INF-4321).

katie (sre): I'll add the AZ-distribution and canary requirements to the ticket. Also flagging that if they want per-route SLA in the contract we need to pin a model version and quantization profile (can't switch flavors without re-approval).

maria (sales): Awesome — I'll paste the snippet and notes into Mediflow's security questionnaire and link INF-4321. Owner: devon to finalize numbers and sign. Meeting with Mediflow scheduled Thu 9am PT to review. :thumbsup:
